newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia to promote its coffee at U.S. conference.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia to promote its coffee at U.S. conference.

text.p: Ethiopian private coffee exporters will participate at a speciality coffee conference in the U.S. in April as part of a strategy to promote Ethiopia's top quality coffee varieties to international consumers.
Aschenaki Gebreheiwot, executive secretary of the private Ethiopian Coffee Association, told Reuters on Wednesday that 20 exporters would be going to New Orleans, Florida, this year.
"Ethiopia will have a stand at the conference where coffee experts and consumers from all over the world will have a chance to sample our top quality coffee varieties," Aschenaki said.
Aschenaki said Ethiopia was present at the Florida gathering last year and generated substantial market interest.
He added that Ethiopian coffee appealed to American and European consumers.
"The bulk of Ethiopian coffee comes from naturally grown and self-sown coffee forests which do not require pesticides or other chemicals and fertiliser," he told Reuters.
Aschenaki said private Ethiopian exporters planned to tour Europe, Asia and the Middle East in their effort to expand their markets for prime washed arabicas.
Private exporters hope to export up to 60,000 tonnes out of a total 108,000 tonnes of exports in 1996/97.
Ethiopian coffee authorities have said they exported over 40,000 tonnes in the first quarter of the crop year.
Ethiopia exported 102,000 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96 and earned $279.5 million --- less than the $300.9 million it received for exporting 78,420 tonnes in 1994/95 because of weaker world prices.
Aschenaki said the Association maintained good relations with the country's coffee authorities.
He said the Association was setting up its own centre to help the private sector meet high quality standards.
Aschenaki said Ethiopian coffee authorities had instituted strict quality controls on all exportable coffee.
The Association, formed 30 years ago and revived after the rise to power of the Meles Zenawi-led administration in 1991, has 50 members.
